samples.summary: Re-running every red CI run for the head SHA erases agent-iterate-ci's "unforgeable" attempt bound, and the verb's own summary still claims the bound is not reset
samples.evidence: agent-iterate-ci.yml:171-174 bounds the autonomous CI-fix loop by counting `r.conclusion === 'failure'` over the branch's ci.yml runs, and its comment calls that count unforgeable because "Actions run history is append-only and the agent cannot delete it". A re-run does not create a new run — this PR's own checks.mjs:70-72 states GitHub bumps `run_attempt` on the existing run and its `conclusion` reflects the latest attempt. The new loop at agent-rerun.yml:204 (and agent-loop.yml:160) re-runs EVERY red completed run for the head SHA, so each one that passes flips `failure` → `success` and drops out of `failedCi`. Where the old `per_page: 1` code could at most rewrite the single newest run, the delta rewrites all of the current head's failure history at once, lowering `failedCi` below MAX_ATTEMPTS and re-arming the fixer past its intended cap. The summary this same step emits (agent-rerun.yml:223-225) still tells the maintainer "the CI-fix arm's own attempt bound (counted from prior failed CI runs) is NOT reset" — a safety claim the change makes false, which is worse than an undocumented weakening because a human reads it and believes it.

samples.summary: The re-run selection is scoped only by workflow file and head SHA — not by head repository, event, or PR — so a maintainer verb can re-run workflow runs belonging to a fork/unrelated branch that merely shares the commit
samples.evidence: `github.paginate(github.rest.actions.listWorkflowRuns, { workflow_id: 'ci.yml', head_sha: pr.head.sha })` (agent-loop.yml:155-157, agent-rerun.yml:199-201) returns every ci.yml run in the base repository with that head SHA, including runs created by fork `pull_request` events — a fork PR's run lives in the base repo and carries the fork's head SHA. Because git SHAs are content-addressed, any unprivileged user can `git fetch` the agent PR's branch, push the identical commits to their fork and open a PR at main, producing a run whose `head_sha` is byte-identical to the agent PR's head. The delta then loops `reRunWorkflow` over every such red run with the job's `actions: write`, so a maintainer typing `@claude loop`/`@claude rerun` re-executes an unrelated (and untrusted-contributor-owned) workflow run they never asked about; the loop is also unbounded in count, one API write per matching run. The same SHA collision feeds the gate side: mark-ready.mjs:131-138 lists runs by `head_sha` with no head-repository filter and now requires ALL of them green (checks.mjs:84-89), so an outsider's same-SHA red run pins gate 1 red — promotion denial from an unprivileged position, exactly the class the panel's concurrency comment (agent-review-panel.yml:82-90) treats as a security requirement — and this delta, the designated remedy, cannot clear it (re-running a stranger's fork run does not make it the PR's evidence and may 403). Downstream damage is limited because agent-review-panel.yml:167 and agent-iterate-ci.yml:56 both require `head_repository.full_name == github.repository`, which is why confidence is low rather than higher; filtering the listed runs to `head_repository.full_name === `${owner}/${repo}`` and/or the PR's own branch would close it.

samples.summary: `conclusion !== 'success'` treats an approval-pending / `action_required` run as "red" and re-runs it, which is the fork-approval surface
samples.evidence: `ciRunsToRerun` (checks.mjs:121-125) and both inline mirrors select re-run candidates as any completed run whose conclusion is not `success`. GitHub uses `action_required` as both a status and a conclusion, and a run gated by the "require approval for fork PRs" setting or an environment protection rule can surface as completed with `conclusion: 'action_required'`. Re-running such a run through the maintainer-privileged `actions: write` step is the API path that would launch untrusted contributor code the approval gate deliberately parked. In practice GitHub answers 403 for a run that still needs approval, so this is a hardening point rather than a demonstrated bypass — but the selection rule is written as "everything that is not success" rather than an allow-list of genuinely re-runnable conclusions (`failure`, `cancelled`, `timed_out`, `startup_failure`), so it will pick up any future conclusion value including approval-gated ones.

verdict.reason: The described code exists exactly as quoted (agent-rerun.yml:199-207 re-runs every red completed ci.yml run for the head SHA; agent-loop.yml:155-163 mirrors it; the summary at agent-rerun.yml:223-225 still claims the CI-fix attempt bound is not reset; agent-iterate-ci.yml:171-174 counts conclusion==='failure' and calls that bound unforgeable). It is nonetheless not a Security-lens defect. (1) No privilege boundary is crossed: both re-run blocks sit behind a Bot filter (agent-rerun.yml:27-31, agent-loop.yml:24-28) and an authoritative write-access gate that setFailed's unless the commenter is admin/maintain/write (agent-rerun.yml:74-85, agent-loop.yml:62-73). The adversary the "unforgeable" comment names is the agent itself ("unlike a PR-comment counter it holds issues:write over", agent-iterate-ci.yml:167-170), and the agent - a Bot without repo write - cannot reach either call site. The only actor who can is a maintainer who could produce the identical effect by clicking "Re-run failed jobs" in the Actions UI, so the change confers no capability anyone lacked. (2) The promotion gate is not weakened: ciConclusion (checks.mjs:84-89) still requires every run on the SHA to have concluded success, and a re-run only flips a run green if CI genuinely passes, so no greenness is forged. (3) What remains is an autonomous-loop attempt budget that a fully privileged human's explicit re-engage action can decrement, plus a now-inaccurate sentence in the summary it emits - a correctness/doc-accuracy concern, not authorization, secrets, injection, crypto/auth, SSRF, deserialization or path traversal, which is the whole of this lane. Deferred to the correctness/docs lenses.

verdict.reason: The quoted code exists verbatim and unfiltered. agent-loop.yml:155-157 and agent-rerun.yml:199-201 list ci.yml runs by head_sha only (no head_repository/event/branch scoping) and loop every non-success completed run into reRunWorkflow (agent-loop.yml:160-163, agent-rerun.yml:204-206) using the job's actions: write (agent-loop.yml:55). ci.yml:9-10 triggers on pull_request against main, so a fork PR's run lives in the BASE repo with the fork's head SHA; because commits are content-addressed, an unprivileged user can push the agent PR's identical commits to a fork and open a PR to produce a base-repo ci.yml run with a byte-identical head_sha, which then enters this unfiltered set. A grep for head_repository across .github/workflows shows the only fork checks are on the subject PR (agent-loop.yml:116-122, agent-rerun.yml:129-142) or on downstream workflow_run triggers (agent-review-panel.yml:167, agent-iterate-ci.yml:56) — none filters the listed runs, so 'already-guarded' does not apply. The gate half is equally present: mark-ready.mjs:131 lists runs by head_sha with no head-repository filter and mark-ready.mjs:138 feeds them to ciConclusion, which at checks.mjs:84-89 requires ALL runs green (and returns null if any conclusion is missing), so a stranger's same-SHA run denies promotion from an unprivileged position. Not-present and out-of-scope both fail: untrusted-party control over what a privileged actions:write job re-executes, and unprivileged denial of a merge gate, are access-control/untrusted-input issues in this lens's lane. Exploitability of the compute-abuse half rests on standard GitHub fork-PR behavior, which is why the reviewer's own confidence was low, but that uncertainty keeps the finding rather than dropping it.

finding.summary: The panel/fix triggers still identify CI by display NAME, so the forged-'CI' run the delta defends mark-ready against still drives agent jobs that push commits
finding.evidence: The delta hardens the READ side (mark-ready/set-state now match `.github/workflows/ci.yml` by path) but leaves every TRIGGER side name-based: `.github/workflows/agent-review-panel.yml:27-28` (`workflow_run: workflows: ["CI"]`) and `.github/workflows/agent-iterate-ci.yml:20-21` (same). The `ci` job then polls only the triggering run id and exports its conclusion (lines 267-328), which is what `if:` gates the `fix` job at line 1627 — the arm that runs the agent and PUSHES a commit to the PR branch. A second workflow file with `name: CI` (the exact forgery CI_WORKFLOW_PATH's comment describes) therefore still: (a) starts the review panel with an attacker-chosen conclusion, and (b) by concluding `failure`, drives agent-iterate-ci's pushing arm — bypassing the 'CI conclusion is a MUTEX between the two pushing arms' invariant documented in checks.mjs:112-119, and doing so even while the real CI run is red or still in flight. Promotion itself remains gated by mark-ready's path check, so this is agent-invocation/mutex abuse rather than a promotion bypass; I could not fully confirm GitHub's matching behaviour when two workflow files share a `name:`. Fix: add `github.event.workflow_run.path == '.github/workflows/ci.yml'` to the `gate`/`ci` job `if:` in both workflows.

verdict.reason: The finding claims both agent workflows identify CI only by display name, letting a forged 'name: CI' run start the review panel and drive agent-iterate-ci's pushing arm. The repository already contains the exact guard the finding proposes. In agent-review-panel.yml the `gate` job's `if:` (lines 164-169) asserts `github.event.workflow_run.path == '.github/workflows/ci.yml'` plus the head-repository check, and lines 156-163 document precisely this display-name forgery. Every downstream job is gated on it: `ci` (277-278), `deps` (344-345), `review-panel` (374-375), and the `contents: write` pushing arm `fix` (1638-1641, needs review-panel and ci, no always()/!cancelled()). A skipped `gate` skips `ci`/`review-panel`, so `fix` is never eligible (needs.ci.outputs.conclusion is empty too). `stalled` (2322-2331) is `!cancelled()` but requires gate.result == 'failure' or managed == 'true', neither of which a skipped gate produces. agent-iterate-ci.yml mirrors this: `gate` if: (52-56) asserts the ci.yml path, failure conclusion, and base-repo head, and the pushing `iterate` job is needs: [gate] with if: needs.gate.outputs.managed == 'true' (86-91). The panel's concurrency key (line 117) also routes non-ci.yml paths to a noop group. The claimed bypass chain is unreachable.
